result.title: When Is the Expensive Method Worth It? A Content-Driven Analysis of Classical Bayer Demosaicing
result.summary: Demosaicing reconstructs a full-colour image from a single-sensor colour-filter-array (CFA) mosaic, where only one colour is measured per pixel. Classical methods make different assumptions about images, from simple averaging to directional edge-aware interpolation, and the directional methods cost markedly more compute. We ask a practical question that a per-image quality ranking does not answer: for a given image, is the expensive directional method worth its cost? Using a controlled simulate-reconstruct pipeline on 80 benchmark images from four public datasets (Kodak, McMaster, BSD100, Urban100), six classical methods, and image-content descriptors fixed before any results were seen, we show that the quality gain of the edge-aware method (Menon 2007) over the best cheap linear method is not constant. It ranges from $-6.6$ to $+6.8$ dB, and on 31% of images it is zero or negative, meaning a cheap method matches or beats the expensive one. The gain is also predictable from content: it correlates with mean image saturation at $r=-0.86$ ($p<10^{-6}$). We then build an interpretable depth-2 decision tree that recommends the best cheap method from image descriptors, beating an always-pick-the-most-common baseline by 20.0 percentage points under leave-one-image-out validation. The analysis uses no deep learning, and every step can be inspected.

AI.brief_summary: 在80张基准图像上比较六种经典 Bayer 去马赛克方法，量化边缘感知昂贵方法相对最佳廉价线性方法的逐图像质量增益，并用预先固定的图像内容描述子（如平均饱和度）与深度2决策树预测该增益是否为正。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「用内容描述子预判昂贵计算是否值得」的轻量决策线索，可供核查 LVR 中按需触发昂贵推理模块或额外计算步的内容判据；但任务与模态差异大，迁移性仅属推测。
